culture: San Miguel has a parish church (la parroquia) that is the town's iconic landmark and turns golden at sunset
El Mirador is a lookout point with a view over the whole city
Locals gather on benches at the lookout to watch the sunset, a cherished daily ritual
Cobblestone streets (calles de piedra) are typical of the historic downtown (el centro)
Carpenters traditionally made handcrafted wooden doors and chairs for the houses in the town center
Church bells and pink evening skies are part of town life and childhood memories
Older Mexicans commonly bless people when saying goodbye: 'que Dios lo bendiga'
Elders address young people warmly as 'joven' and use polite 'usted' with strangers
Friendly strangers readily strike up conversation and invite you to sit with them or join them
'Hasta mañana' is the way to say see you tomorrow
Phrases like 'se me hace un nudo en la garganta' (a lump in my throat) express deep emotion
Folk wisdom is passed down from fathers, e.g. 'el sol no se compra, solo se espera'
